title: Late interrupt exit code preservation in Command.main
answers: How does Click ensure late interrupts do not change the command exit code?
What policy governs KeyboardInterrupt during Command.main teardown?
Where is exit code preservation enforced for late SIGINT in Click?
body:
In src/click/core.py:Command.main, late interrupts (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError) occurring after command completion or during reporting must preserve the intended exit code in standalone mode.
Handlers must defer message display and termination to teardown by storing a report callable and exit_code, rather than invoking sys.exit() or output routines directly.
Enforced in src/click/core.py:Command.main by wrapping the final report() and sys.exit(exit_code) invocation in an outer try...except block.
What breaks if skipped: A second Ctrl-C during error output or an interrupt during exit after success leaks an unhandled traceback and fails to return the intended exit status.
applies: CLI process teardown and exception handling in src/click/core.py:Command.main
says: Cancelling terminal output during shutdown changes the tool's intended return exit code.
Hitting interrupt while an error displays must preserve the original failure status code.
Automated scripts miss command failures if the user presses interrupt while printing errors.
Ensure interrupting a finished command never overwrites its final exit code in scripts.
Terminal return code should not get corrupted if cancelled during the closing summary.
